geeklist.title: BGG.CON Virtual Flea Market 2023
geeklist.description:
[center][COLOR=#009933][size=18][b]Virtual Flea Market 2023 - CLOSED[/b][/size][/COLOR]
See 2024: [geeklist=342440][/geeklist]
[size=14][b]PLEASE READ THIS ENTIRE HEADER!! I made the description more concise this year![/b][/size][/center]
[u][b]Room Plan[/b][/u] Everyone who sold 8 or more games has at least half a table. I have managed to combine tables so that a table only has two sellers, with a few only having one seller if they sold a lot of games. Tables are sorted by username. Average of 50 games sold per table. [b]Please, please, please be patient and help others. We have to make sure this goes smoothly so that we do not get restricted in the future. This is the largest VFM ever! [/b]Here are the assignments: [center][imageid=7847029 large inline][/center] Here is another format of the [b]Exact same thing.[/b](If I got it wrong, well, I guess tell me.) This is in a format for the geek squad to check in people and another way to find a table. Let me know what you think. This might be easier to use.: [center][imageid=7847789 large inline][/center][/q]
[b][u]CHANGE:[/u][/b] [b]The tables in the room will be arranged by the sellers username [/b] again. Since we just assign tables to the top [-]80 [/-] 138 people who have sold games, generally if you sold 10 games or more you should have a table. I will have signs on the tables so it is easy to see them. See [url=https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Stats/321725]https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Stats/321725[/url] for the list of sold items.
[u][b]General[/b][/u] Here is the concept - For people who are travelling to the convention, sellers only want to bring games that they have sold. Buyers want to plan how much space they need to bring games home. Enter the Virtual Flea Market. If you have items that you'd like to sell at BGG.Con, list them here with the condition of your items, and the price or terms you'd like to sell for. Buyers settle on a price with the seller. At the con, buyers give an envelope with pre-counted money to the seller who hands them the game!
[b]Coordination:[/b] I (Sterling Babcock, Solamar) will be running the Virtual Flea Market and attending. My wife, Marcia (RedPhoenixNia) will also be helping me as well as Team Geek. [b]Date & Location: [/b] Held in Reunion EFGH Thursday evening (6p-7p VFM Seller Setup, 7p-8p VFM). Enter from the 3 doors in the hall. * Please send your [b]thanks to Jeff Anderson[/b] and the BGG.CON team for continuing to have the VFM for 2023! * Please be [b]polite and courteous[/b] in all your communication. * We won't be requiring masks but do recommend them in this crowded situation. Please remember [url=https://tabletop.events/conventions/bgg.con-2023/pages/health-safety-guide][b]BGG.CON's Health & Safety Guidelines[/b][/url]: "Respect the personal choices of those around you. [url=https://tabletop.events/conventions/bgg.con-2023/pages/code-of-conduct63][b]We will not tolerate harassment of any kind[/b][/url], and this now explicitly includes the choice to wear or not wear a mask."
[u][b]Seller Guidelines[/b][/u] * There are 80 tables. [b]Change: There will be no sign up for sellers tables.[/b] I will assign a "Sellers" ticket for one 6'x30" table to each top seller. (e.g. if you sell approximately 10 games or more you will get a table. (e.g. No one gets a table without selling games, which was a problem last year.) If you do not get a ticket because you sold too few games, you are on your own to arrange the exchange. * You are expected to [u]be at your sellers table for the full hour[/u] or until your games are sold. If you want to be a buyer, make other time arrangements to do your pickups outside the VFW event, or have another person do your pickups during the VFW. * Anyone with a BGG.CON badge may participate in the VFM. If you do not plan to attend the VFM for pickup, make that clear to your buyers in your listing. * [b]The tables in the room will be arranged by the sellers username. [/b] * [u]Do NOT delete your item[/u]. People expect the numbers not to change. If you remove an item, Mark them as sold or no longer available. * Please do add your items to this list! You choose how to sell your items: Fixed Price, Auction, Dutch Auction. You should monitor your own items. * Sellers: List Aggregator Tools: - If your item is an auction, please include the word "[b]Auction[/b]" someplace. (It helps the aggregator tools) - If you are selling an item that deserves an [b]alternate name[/b] in a summary list (i.e. Misc Game Accessory), please place this code in your item someplace: "+altname+ Whatever You'd Like To Call Your Item -altname-" - [u]Mark sold items as: SOLD so that the summary tools[/u] can remove it from the available list. Mark who purchased it as well. - If you change your price, [u]please keep the new price on the same line of the geeklist[/u] (Do something like $25 $20) * There is an [u]easy way to add items[/u] to the geeklist, courtesy of Eric Bettan (Carnage994): Alphabetical search tool: https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/321725 The link to add games is: https://yulgame.com/Vfm/AddItems/321725 * Sellers with tickets will be allowed into the room to set up between 6-6:45pm on Thursday evening. No games will be allowed into the room after 6:45 pm. Sellers stay on INSIDE of tables. Do NOT block the outside traffic with games! * You [u]may NOT use hotel luggage carts[/u]. * Sellers should arrange a bulk commission at the BGG Marketplace * Any attempt by a seller to deceive a buyer by significantly miss describing the item (e.g. missing stated expansion) will be dealt with harshly. * Please be kind, bring a sign, and try to help each other out.
[u][b]Buyers Guidelines[/b][/u] * You may not enter before 7 pm. PLEASE BE PROMPT at 7 pm!! We have to be clear of the room by no later than 8 pm to make room for other BGG events. * Buyers MUST attend the START of the hour of exchange and stay until all your games are received. Do NOT be late and make people wait for you! Buyers are REQUIRED to either show up, or notify the Seller they will not be there. Do NOT be 'that guy' which makes a seller wait all hour trying to find you. You must find the seller! * Buyers stay on the OUTSIDE of the tables for ease of finding games. * If you are a [b]buyer[/b], please bring one envelope for each seller you are buying from. [b]Each envelope should be marked on the outside with the seller's user name, and the items you are buying and should contain exact change![/b] After doing this for a few years, we can tell you that this makes the event go much more smoothly for everyone. * The room will be organized according to Sellers' [b]User Names - This may change this year. Still investigating![/b]. * Any attempt by a buyer to deceive the seller and pick up a game which you did not rightfully purchase will be dealt with harshly. * Failure to follow these rules may cause you to be rejected from future Virtual Flea Markets.
[u][b]Expectations[/b][/u] Since this event has gotten so large (also fun and successful), we need everyone's help to keep the event organized so we can continue it in future years. Please be on time. Please be considerate to the several hundred other people that are participating so this can continue to be a great experience! There is nothing more frustrating that walking through the room looking for someone, only to find out they are running late or wandering about the hall looking for their own pickups.
[u][b]Summary of Unsold Games[/b] - Use one of these links for an alphabetized list of games still available[/u] Alphabetical search tool courtesy of Eric Bettan (Carnage994): https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/321725
Here’s another search list function by David Rathbun: https://sunderedrealm.com/bgg/bgg-list.php?l=321725
[u][b]Request List[/b][/u] If there is something you are looking for, think about adding it to Virtual Flea Market for Delivery to BGG.Con 2023 - Request List. [geeklist=322056][/geeklist]
[u][b]Shipping Games[/u][/b]: See the BGG.CON Master list for FedEx delivery information.
[u][b]Math Trade[/b][/u] If you participate in the BGG.Con Math Trade, please make sure that items are NOT listed in both at the same time. However, this will not be monitored. So if you do so, it is your responsibility to immediately mark items sold as no longer available in the Math trade, and mark them deleted from this list if they are traded. If you make a mistake and sell a game twice, it is your responsibility to fulfill all your commitments, no matter what the cost is to you. It is far better that you avoid conflicts like this.
[u][b]BGG.CON Bazaar Marketplace[/b][/u] The BGG.CON Bazaar Marketplace is a separate event run at 10 am on Friday, where you can explore and purchase games at the con. It is not related to the Virtual Flea Market, but please do attend!
[u][b]Tuesday Night Meetup[/b][/u] BGG.Con staff has advised me that since they do not officially take any hotel space on Tuesday, there can be no official or unofficial events prior to Wednesday.
[u][b]Tips from Past Sellers[/b][/u]: 1. Create a spreadsheet with the games your selling. Create columns for Game Name, Game Cost, Method of Payment, Buyer Name, Buyer BGG Name, Comments, etc. If you’re paying via PayPal, Venmo, etc. make a note. Print off your list prior to the event and bring it with you. 2. Send out geek mails and confirm with the game sale with people who have bought games from you. Sometimes people miss responses to game transactions. 3. Have a full-length, printed sheet with your Tabletop.events Name, BGG User Name, and Avatar/Logo on it for people to find you more easily. 4. Print out the table assignments beforehand. Circle your table. 5. Removable Sticky notes on the game with the name of the Buyer picking up your games would be helpful. 6. Please [u]get your money out of the envelopes[/u] and deposit the empty envelopes in the trash. Please do not leave it for staff to clean up!
[u][b]Tips from Past Buyers[/b][/u]: 1. Create a spreadsheet with the games you're buying. Create columns for Game Name, Game Cost, Method of Payment, Seller Tabletop Events Name, Seller BGG Name, Comments, etc. If you're paying via PayPal, Venmo, etc. make a note. Print off your list prior to the event and bring it with you. 2. Buy plain envelopes. Write down the name of each game you’re buying and the name of the Seller. [u]Provide exact change.[/u] Put your name on your envelopes so it's easily identified as paid by sellers or in case it gets lost. 4. Bring plenty of bags to haul off your 'new' games. You won't be able to use the luggage carts.

I did put sold in the comments and marked my games as sold, yet it shows the Buyer as N/A. What am I doing

[q="Maucoin"]I did put sold in the comments and marked my games as sold, yet it shows the Buyer as N/A. What am I doing [/q] You need to put the sold information, with the buyer's username into the **body** of the Geeklist item. For example, on your [listitem=10096944]Clocktowers[/listitem] item, You can click on the username of your buyer and copy his link "https://boardgamegeek.com/user/mrdrofficer" from the browser address bar. Go back to edit the Geeklist item and add the line "Sold for $3 to " and then click the link icon (looks like two chain link at a 45 degree angle) and paste the user link into the "paste any link" box then click "next" and "add link".
The result looks like this "Sold for $3 to [user=mrdrofficer][/user]" in the body of the Geeklist item. This will allow the indexer to pick up the username.
Personally, I like to strike out the rest of the text also. You can see one of my sold items [listitem=10086091]here[/listitem] as an example.
Thankyou!

How long should it take for the seller to respond to offers? (Excepting those that states that we will close the bid in by a certain date or month).

[q="DomerHoo"]How long should it take for the seller to respond to offers? (Excepting those that states that we will close the bid in by a certain date or month).[/q]
Honestly, 10++ years of selling if it hasn't moved in a week I let it go for offered price or keep it for the next VFM. I think most people are like me. I don't look backwards, usually only scanning new posts added. I figure if I past it and didn't bite to bad. Rarely do I wait a few days or back track.

Derek as a seller and buyer I can say that generally if I don't respond to your offer within 24h (maybe longer on a weekend) it means I'm not going to accept the offer. Some sellers will wait though until the last few days before the convention and try to counter offer/accept as no one else was interested.

i feel like even if i plan to wait or don't want the offer it's much nicer to just respond and say such a thing rather than just leaving it open.
As a buyer if i don't have a response in a couple days i just assume it's not sold if it's something im ok with my offer sitting out there and the seller eventuallys gets back to me i'll consider it at that point on if i still want it for that price or not.

For me, I think there should be a response even if it is a no. If I don't respond to an offer or even a BIN then I probably missed the ping and I don't want to forget to pack any sold games! I always try to follow up in a geekmail before the con with any purchases I made and sold items to buyers with totals and games. It is always good to double-check!

i used to always respond, but one year I had a tire kicker make low ball offers (in general 50% less than my asking price), on over 50 games, after that I just gave up on responding frequently. so I normally only respond maybe once a week (sometimes not at all).

from past experience (I have rented the largest SUV I could and stuffed it full of games for a return drive, when I used to live in Austin. Biggest year was 135 games for me and about 40 games for a local friend. Another year we filled the rental SUV, my car, and had a friend put 1 box of games in the back of his car to help get it back to the house. filling boxes wastes a lot of space, if I would have just stacked the games up i could have fit them all in the SUV.
That being said, a common thing people do at Essen is pack boxes inside of boxes, so bring Ziplock's to keep contents of each game separate then combine multiple Ziplock's into 1 larger box, and stack tiered (Russian doll style) boxes inside other empty boxes. I saw a person fit 74!!! games into their 2 suit cases that way one year.
I'm just going the semi expensive way and shipping mine back

For the various list aggregator tools adding the tag [c]+sold+[/c] to your listing is a more reliable way of marking something sold. It's not likely to occur without purpose or intent. Or if the item was removed the tag [c]+remove+[/c] will hide it on the same tools.

Per the rules:
* You are expected to be at your sellers table for the full hour or until your games are sold. If you want to be a buyer, make other time arrangements to do your pickups outside the VFW event, or have another person do your pickups during the VFW.
The best solution would be to either find another person selling at the vfm and combine tables so you can trade off who is there, arrange your pickups outside vfm time, or find a friend who can help you. Because you don't want to wait till 5 min before and try and run around and get all your games.

Helpful observation:
I have noticed SEVERAL prices on the indexes with incorrect prices, because there are multiple prices within a listing on different lines of the entry. You might be mentioning a different related item, a bundle, etc.
If you put multiple prices in your listing, the index may show $50 cost for a $10 item.
Also remember that if you have the word "SOLD" anywhere in the listing, the index marks your item as SOLD.

[q="Sassyoneforu"]Dumb question! I'm listing games for first time. I have some pictures I wanted to include, but not sure how. I was reading the formatting help and not sure how to proceed. So, my dumb question is I have the pictures on my C drive, but examples look like they are on the internet somewhere. How do I get them attached? I'm sure it's something simple and I'm being a dummy. Appreciate the help!
PS - I pushed us over 9900! Only 996 to go![/q]
Choose the blue + to add an item to the geeklist. Select the name of the game you want to add. 7 icons will show above where you enter your text. If you let your most hover over the fifth one, a tooltip will appear that says "Embed Media". Select that. Another little menu bar will appear. Select the leftmost option called "image". An "Embed Image" window will open. The file menu at the top of this window will have three options: Geek Image, External Image, Upload Image. Select Upload Image. Then choose the the "Browse" button to navigate to the picture on your computer that you want to upload. Select "Upload & Embed Image.

Buyers, please be conscientious of the games you claim. Although no money has exchanged hands, sellers count these sales as if they happened. That's why they are marked as sold immediately and removed from the listings.
Canceling a sale within a few days might not matter much, because there is still time for others to see it's available, but canceling a sale weeks or months later sucks. Not only is the seller losing out on that exposure time, but some ppl "hide" postings that have been sold, or more realistically, that game is now buried behind 50+ pages that most likely will not have any eye traffic.
It's happened to me a couple times during this VFM, and it isn't fair to the seller who is basically just waiting for the con to collect.

[q="CheddarLimbo"]2 Q's - (1) Do I need to do something specific for a newly posted item to show up on the yulgame.com tracker list thingy?[/q] The challenge with a list this large is BGG has difficultly serving it up. They don't provide a feature to bring the list into chunks, so any tool (like the yulgame one or the one I host at sunderedrealm) has to wait and wait and sometimes wait some more to get results. 🙂 The yulgame list looks like they have implemented a caching system where they retrieve the list and store the data, and then go back periodically to get updates, rather than trying to retrieve the list live every time. I plan to implement something similar but haven't gotten around to it.
Bottom line - you do not have to do anything to get the items to show up, other than wait for a refresh to happen on the remote site.

I agree with @kitfox4, mostly. Off the top of my head:
• The VFM seems great for doing win-wins: sellers make money and get rid of stuff; buyers get to save money and maybe try new games they wouldn't otherwise, or find something off their wishlist. • What about a deadline for qualifying for tables in the VFM? That could be as soon as now. Next year, just make it a week earlier. • Like kitfox4 said, people in this day and age can easily make their own arrangements if they didn't qualify for a table by the deadline. We're adults with cell phones. People are friendly. • Similarly, I can see this VFM still useful during the con, especially after the Bazaar! People will want to sell the stuff that didn't sell there, so just leaving this list up and functional gives them something better than nothing. Or maybe people bought too much and realize they can't pack it all, so they want to find a good home for the overflow. • BTW, I wish the thread about the VFM were pinned. Why isn't it? I wouldn't have seen it because it's not on the first page of BGG.CON threads, except for Jonathan's Unofficial catch-all thread. Is there any way the VFM could last longer, in future years, like 2-3 hours, so that folks have ample time to meet up there regardless of whether they have a table or not?

if memory serves, the reason it's limited to 2 hours (1 hour set up and 1 hour sales/breakdown) is the room is used for other items. Also many sellers want to get back to gaming after taking a 2-3 hour break to sell games. As a person that for several years purchased over 100 games on the VFM its possible to get them all in that time, but you need to hussle and it helps if you can pick stuff up early from sellers/deliver to buyers early as well.

The 2 hour limit is due to the room being needed for other things, just like the Bazaar is limited. I don’t want to be the seller that ends up waiting on THAT GUY who meanders in at the 115 minute mark to pick up his game.

The first year that there was an organized meetup it was longer if I remember correctly. Waaaaay fewer people, but with it being that long, a lot of people didn't show up until halfway through, and there was chaos - a lot of people walking around shouting out usernames. Keeping it to an hour is a decent compromise, and it tends to die down relatively quickly. This year is on a whole new level though, so I guess we shall see.
There's nothing stopping anyone from planning to meet up with people right after the VFM time (just not in the VFM room)

easily. My suggestions:
1) First see if anyone is available before the event (often you can get upwards of 20-30% of your games pre-VFM time depending on the seller. Sometimes they will bring games down with them when they are gaming if you arrange a time to swing past a table and grab them/pay them. 2) bring a helper to pack up your games 3) have something to carry games so you can carry more than a handful at a time (be it a box, a boardgame storage bag, etc. 4) have all of your money pre-sorted into envelops listing the seller and the games you are getting from them. And have them in alpha order so you can just go down your list and if seller x isnt at their table you move on to the next table.

Just give your friend half the envelopes and a copy of your spreadsheet. And a person can carry only so many games anyway. Three people would be 3x efficient. It scales linearly, right? Here's another (parallel) idea: I'm staying at the Hyatt for the first time; I presume people can go up the elevators without a room key? If so, those staying in the Hyatt can hold "office hours" before VFM, if they like. For example, if I were selling, I would let all my buyers know that on Wed from X–Y (30' window), I'll be in room X if they want to get their stuff then. Similarly, if I were buying, I would let my sellers know similarly. I can find something to do while chilling in my room for 30', and no one is forced to come. The virtual flea market is a great opportunity for board game enthusiasts to buy, sell, and trade games. It is particularly useful for those traveling to conventions, as they can list the games they want to sell and buyers can plan how much space they need to bring games home. The virtual flea market is run by Sterling Babcock and is a professional and well-organized event. To list games on the virtual flea market, one must first register with Board Game Geek and then go to the virtual flea market's geek list for the specific convention. They can then add their game to the list with its name, image, description, price, condition, and payment types accepted. Both buyers and sellers can negotiate on prices, and buyers can also use the "buy it now" option to purchase games at a set price without haggling. Sellers can use various resources to determine the prices of their games, such as the price history on Board Game Geek, Amazon, and other online resources. The virtual flea market also has a search function that allows buyers to search for games and see what is available and what has been sold. Overall, the virtual flea market is a great opportunity for board game enthusiasts to buy, sell, and trade games in a convenient and organized manner.
Bullet Summary: - Virtual flea market is an opportunity to buy, sell, and trade games - Useful for those traveling to conventions - Buyers can plan how much space they need to bring games home - Sterling Babcock runs a professional and well-organized event - To list games, one must register with Board Game Geek and add their game to the specific convention's geek list - Both buyers and sellers can negotiate on prices - Sellers can use various resources to determine game prices - Virtual flea market has a search function for buyers to see what is available and what has been sold.

[q="Sportomax"]Not sure if this is the correct forum but thought I would check. Does anyone have traveling recommendations or experience for buying or selling large volume of games at conventions? Tempted to use suitcase but figured others might have more reasonably creative ideas. Boxes, bags, wagons? Not sure how much I trust airlines with checked baggage outside of suitcases though. Thanks in advance for the input. [/q] it depends on how much you bought/sold. Generally speaking some options:
buying 1) bring ziplocks of various sized and combine games in boxes and nest them all tetris style within your suitcase you would be surpised how many games you can fit that way (can easily hit max weight and have space left) 2) if you dont mind the expense (ask vendors if they have any empty bulk game (case) boxes you can have or stop at a home depot/etc, box the games up and ship home via UPS/Fedex, the con normally has a vendor there for shipping (it can be expensive though) 3) for transporting within the hotel (folding wagon/dolly/etc. boardgame travel bags (generally hold 6+ games per full load)
selling (for transport) 1) not much you can do with shipping them to the con outside of stuffing your bags, getting a refinforced box from home depot and packing it tight with games and hoping it doesnt get too damaged and checking the box at the airport) 2) have someone to help you carry your boxes down to the VFM/bazar to sell) 3) having a folding wagon/dolly/etc.

I have used a few different methods over the years. :meeple:
Car: I used to love my totes, but the ones I had did not fit effectively in my car. Now I prefer cardboard boxes. I ask my local FLGS for boxes about a month prior, offering to come pick them up at their convenience. These are often ideal because they are board-game sized. Boxes make stacking and packing them for car transport ideal. You can also find sturdy boxes at liquor stores, but most are smaller.
At the hotel, I now use two methods: Method 1 - I also own a Cosco (NOT Costco) Shifter collapsible cart. It converts to either a traditional tall dolley or a flatbed, which is how I use it for Bazaar and VFM. It is $60-80 and available on Amazon, and at Home Depot and Target that I know of. I also see that Harbor Freight has one for $40, but I cannot say how it performs.
Method 2 - wheeled suitcases. Just before the Bazaar and VFM, I will pack some of heavier/awkward sized games into my wheeled suitcases. Easy everywhere, especially in the elevator.
Definitely take Jeff and Dwayne seriously: [b]Hotel bellcarts will NOT be available.[/b] as noted in the top post.[/q]

item.body:
[color=#ff5100][b]Auction closed![/b][/color]
Sold for $20.00 to [user=Bentadams1][/user] [-] Lot of Pacesetter/Mayfair Chill RPG items.
This all came from the estate of a deceased friend. My RPG experience is quite old and primarily AD&D so I have no idea what value this has. I'm putting this up as an auction.
Everything is intact (except as noted) and in good condition with some cover wear and general aging. In some of the books, notes are written in, all in fine-tip mechanical pencil and can be erased if desired.
List of contents:
Pacesetter items: * [thing=44649][/thing] - [b]INCOMPLETE [/b]- consists of the box (significant wear and the corners are taped - poor condition), [i]Horrors from the Unknown[/i] book (cover wear, no missing pages) and [i]Campaign Book[/i] (cover wear, no missing pages). Everything else is missing. * [thing=55304][/thing] - small amount of corner wear and creasing. * [thing=44658][/thing] - cover wear; center 4 pages (31-34) were missing, but the text continues straight from page 30 to page 35. I found a double-sheet which appears to have been in the middle of the book, having a page of The Evil Way Disciplines, a page of CHILL Animal Table and two pages of Creature Sheets; I assume this was originally in this book. * [thing=44750][/thing] - Minor cover wear, appears to be complete, spine is intact. * [thing=44752][/thing] - Minor cover wear, appears to be complete, front cover opens flat but otherwise spine is intact.
Mayfair items: * [thing=44622][/thing] - Minor cover wear, appears to be complete, spine is intact. * [thing=44619][/thing] - Minor cover wear, appears to be complete, spine is intact. * A 4-page leaflet titled Chill from Old to New - Creases where it had been tri-folded to fit in a business envelope but otherwise in good condition.
Starting bid: $20.00 Auction will end 11/1/2023 sometime in the evening.

I have the Revised Edition (2nd edition)
I will offer $100. Completely understand if that's not in your comfort zone, but it's the limit of mine. 🙂

[q="drathbun"]I will offer $100. Completely understand if that's not in your comfort zone, but it's the limit of mine. 🙂[/q] Hi there, any thoughts on this? Completely fine if you're not interested at this price point, but if you are declining the offer it frees up some of my budget for other games instead. Right now I have reserved $100 for this in case you are willing to accept. Thanks! :)
So sorry Dave. Figured I didn't need to reply unless I was accepting the offer, I'm going to decline that offer at this time. Thanks for your interest though!
Without a reply, I can't tell the difference between "No, I am declining your offer" and "I haven't considered your offer because I have not read it." 🙂 Thanks for the confirmation.
Hi, Brock, any final thoughts on my $100 offer at this point? 🙂 No worries, if I don't hear back I will assume you decline again. ;)
Hi, Dave. For whatever reason this decision is excruciating to me, so counter offer: Full set for $125 or will split the expansion out for your offer of $100.

I have been trying to keep my spending under my sales. $125 fits, so as long as you are comfortable with that offer I will take it. No problems on my side if you wake up tomorrow and want to retract it. :)

item.body:
2006 English second edition. Complete and in good condition - minor bowing on the box sides (kind of a thin box).
A fantasy medieval territory control game with kind of hex-sudoku/minesweeper math thing going to resolve conflicts. Great Josh Cappel Art.
[b]Mechanics:[/b] Enclosure, Modular Board
[imageid=154658] [b]Buy it now:[/b] $10
[url=https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/321725?Seller=Munin&Status=NotSold]click here to view all my items available for sale[/url]

2009 English edition. Complete with cards in great condition. Box shows light shelf wear (whitening) along edges.
Fun John Kovalic cartoon art illustrating a 2-8 player space war card game. My boys really enjoyed making all the laser blast noises when we played this one.
[b]Mechanics:[/b] Hand Management, Variable Player Powers
[imageid=157567] [b]Buy it now:[/b] $15
[url=https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/321725?Seller=Munin&Status=NotSold]click here to view all my items available for sale[/url]

2007 Rio Grande Games English/French edition. Complete with box and cardboard components in great condition. The poor little mice though are cast white resin almost as fragile as glass. Several have chipped off noses while falling into the deadly pits of the chateau. One even lost an ear the same way. All have been touched up with markers and paint so the injuries are not noticeable.
March your team of mice across the roof of the chateau, questing for cheese while trying to dodge the perilous deadfall pits laid by your opponents. My boys loved this one and delighted in dropping dad's mice into sooo many pits. This one isn't like many others.
[b]Mechanics:[/b] Action Points, Map Deformation, Memory
[imageid=201101]
[b]Buy it now:[/b] [-]$30[/-] Not sold - moved to Math Trade
[url=https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/321725?Seller=Munin&Status=NotSold]click here to view all my items available for sale[/url]

2013 Multilingual first edition. Complete with box and components in great shape.
Thematic abstract strategy game of elemental martial artists. When my boys and I played this, we always started with: [i] Water. Earth. Fire. Air. Long ago, the four nations lived together in harmony. Then, everything changed when the Fire Nation attacked....[/i]
Seriously, someone should license The Last Airbender series and reprint this game. My boys who played chess always enjoyed this one.
[b]Mechanics:[/b] Action Points, Grid Movement
[imageid=2062784] [b]Buy it now:[/b] $25
[url=https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/321725?Seller=Munin&Status=NotSold]click here to view all my items available for sale[/url]

David Sirlin's love letter to Street Fighter, with 20 unique characters from the Fantasy Strike universe. Great chibi style art.

The 3x5 Dutchess table, four cupholders, and topper from the boardgametables.com Kickstarter. Includes two double-sided mats (two blue, one maroon, one burgundy). It's been a great table, we're just looking for something bigger. 🙂

$500 OBO.
[imageid=7752797 medium]
[imageid=7752796 medium]
[imageid=7752798 medium]
[imageid=7752799 medium]
item.comment: What is the outside dimensions of the table?

I believe 3x5. Still considering your offer Tolio as the Con approaches.
It’s this table with added cupholders and a topper: https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/boardgametables/the-duchess-a-gaming-table-from-boardgametablescom
Was just checking was not sure if it was outside dimensions or that was the play area

The Duchess table has a 3 foot by 5 foot playing surface with a 3 inch rail all around it. That makes it 3.5 feet by 5.5 feet total.
incase you were looking for it :)
Danny's asking as were wondering if it will fit in my truck box or not. Can you get the exact measurements from the table?
Been following. Glad someone commented as I couldn't find it. :) So tempted by this.

Yep! I'm working in KC today and tomorrow. I'll try to snag measurements tonight. It comes apart, and I planned to transport it down in a Tesla M3, so a truck shouldn't be any issue. It's really been a great table! For most games (especially 2-3 player) it works really well. For some of the newer sprawling games (Twilight Imperium, Mr. President) or higher player counts (5+) it can be a little tight.
I thought we'd use the topper quite a bit more, but we haven't used it much at all as we have a separate gaming area (from our dining room). It is needed for our Chrokinole board as the board is just an inch or two larger than the table opening.
The table itself has some knicks which were originally a bigger deal, but using a brown marker makes them not noticeable. Nobody else has ever commented on it, it's just something I noticed.

Thanks Zack. My truck box is only 5.5’ long, so I’m trying to figure out if it will fit with the tailgate up. I’m driving down from Canada so having the tailgate up is kind of a big deal 😄
Can you get a measurement on the topper too? My assumption is that each piece is 20” x 68”

Sorry for the delay! The shorter rails are exactly three feet, and the longer rails are 65.5 inches. I'm planning to remove the bolts for transport, so it will be four rails, four legs, and the support/wooden sheet down the middle (along with the rolled up mats).
Thanks for letting me know the dimensions. We're discussing. I suspect the answer is "where would we put it" and "no" and "why are you crying", but it can't hurt to ask 😄
I will offer you $450 for the table

We haven't heard from Zack recently, so I'm posting it here so it's public. Danny's offer above has been recinded. My ability to transport the table back to Canada is gone, as my truck was crushed last weekend. Apologies, the logistics no longer work out 😕
Apologies, I didn’t realize you were waiting on me. So sorry to hear about the crash! 😞

It has the KS cards and all game components. There were some extras as a part of the campaign that were not game components (book marks, stickers, pin......). I still have some of the stickers that will be included in the box. If you would like a picture or anything specific I can verify it is there for you.

Thanks for the confirmation. I'm aware of what came in the KS package, the pink dragon was an add-on (for a small $ or for completing a puzzle). I was curious as to whether that specific item was there. I am not concerned about the stickers. 🙂 I will offer $75 for your consideration; no worries whatsoever if you're not interested in dropping the price that much. If nothing else maybe it will spark an offer from someone else. 😎
I will have to hold off for now but I do appreciate the offer. I will let you know if anything changes.

+remove+ [-]Item: Colosseum (Days of Wonder edition) Condition: NIS Price: $140
Description This is a rare item...a still shrink-wrapped copy of the Days of Wonder edition of Colosseum. The edition in the picture is what I have for sale.
If you are not familiar with the game, it's quite fun! Players bid on resources used to put on a show in the Roman Colosseum. You score your show based on whether you had a complete set of components (did an understudy perform a lead role? were you missing some props?) and who attended (was there a Roman Senator in the audience, perhaps?). Once you score, you select your next show and bid on the components for that. At the end of the game your score is not cumulative...you only score the best performance that you displayed.
Like most older Days of Wonder games the components here are amazing.
I'm willing to listen to offers on this game, but I will tell you I paid close to $170 for this on eBay back when I bought it so that's the starting point and I have already discounted from there. 😉

Description Delivered one of these on eBay for $50+, have another copy and don't know why I didn't list it here first. Yes, there is a new reprint "big box" edition of this game. But if you have the original game and do not have this expansion, here's your chance! The Port expansion replaces the travel component of the game with a (in my opinion) more interesting shipping option, where you are picking up and dropping off goods, plus there is the opportunity to be buried at sea instead of the village chronicle. $40 is the original retail for this expansion, so it's not marked up despite being out of print / unavailable everywhere.

2010 Z-Man edition. Complete with components in great condition and plastic storage boxes for the cards and bits. The box shows wear at the corners and has a crease at one corner on the back (which is as I acquired it a few years ago).
Poseidon is an 18XX-lite game. 18XX are traditionally train games and are generally robust economic endeavors that can be daunting to learn. Poseidon is a great on-ramp to that world with ships instead of trains and simplified mechanics. Check out Bleicher's great evaluation of Poseidon as a way to shepherd your game group into 18XX: [thread=1544990]Why Poseidon works - or How did I successfully enter the 18XX universe[/thread].
[b]Mechanics:[/b] Commodity speculation, Stock holding, Network and route building

item.comment:
From Ted Marshall: “ You need to put the sold information, with the buyer's username into the **body** of the Geeklist item. For example, on your Clocktowers item, You can click on the username of your buyer and copy his link "https://boardgamegeek.com/user/mrdrofficer" from the browser address bar. Go back to edit the Geeklist item and add the line "Sold for $3 to " and then click the link icon (looks like two chain link at a 45 degree angle) and paste the user link into the "paste any link" box then click "next" and "add link".
The result looks like this "Sold for $3 to mrdrofficer Avatar Taylor Hall @mrdrofficer " in the body of the Geeklist item. This will allow the indexer to pick up the username.
Personally, I like to strike out the rest of the text also. You can see one of my sold items here as an example.”
I will update my listings later today to conform to this

I believe "FP" stands for "Fixed Price". It's the option that is populated when you chose not to set your listing up as an option when using "the link to add games is: https://yulgame.com/Vfm/AddItems/321725" listed in the header.

Seems there’s some terminology that would helpful to know… Particularly for new folks
NIS - New in Shrink FP - Fixed Price BIN - Buy It Now VFM - Virtual Flea Market Meetup - When we gather to exchange games

item.objectname: The Castles of Burgundy: Meeple Realty Insert
item.body:
$5 OBO.
I have the large insert for organizing tiles, but not the dice towers.

2008 English first edition. Complete with components in great condition. Box is in good condition, except for a well repaired separated corner (pictured below). I fixed it when I acquired the game used and it's had no further problems.
Great gateway game for worker placement and nominated for a ton of awards over the years. Beautiful Michael Menzel illustrated board and solid hunter-gatherer game play that still holds up. Also includes the fancy leather cup for rolling dice.
[b]Mechanics:[/b] Worker placement, Set Collection, Contracts
[imageid=920102 inline] [imageid=7776038 inline] [imageid=7776037 inline]

item.body:
2015 Z-man English edition. Complete with box and components in great condition.
12th century nobles competing for power across six regions of Europe. It's a layered area majority euro with interesting secondary and tertiary goals, time phased scoring, and a clever turn order mechanic that keeps plans shifting the entire game.
[imageid=2277261] [b]Sold for: [/b]$20 to [user=tovartx4]
item.comment: Such a great game from an underrated designer.
Thanks for the offer, Matt. I quite like this one and I'll hang on to it if it doesn't sell.

item.objectname: Legendary: A Marvel Deck Building Game
item.body:
[B]Version:[/B] English edition (2012) [B]Language:[/B] English [B]Condition:[/B] Like New
Large collection of Legendary. All cards are sleeved (except extras that aren't required--duplicates of base game cards that came in the Marvel Studios Phase I expansion--and the schemes since you only use one per game and they don't need to be shuffled. All cards are in excellent condition.
All cards are stored in a 5 column card storage box as pictured. It is heavy, probably around 30-35 pounds. Includes cardstock printed dividers as pictured with space for more cards or the playmats as shown.
[imageid=7135905 inline][imageid=7135908 inline] Full box and zoomed for detail on dividers.
Includes the following sets in addition to the base game's 500 cards:
[b]Standalone expansions[/b] Large sets of heroes and villains with masterminds and schemes in addition to required starting decks. Each comes with a playmat to use as an alternative to the base game's board. [thing=156689][/thing] (500 cards) [thing=252985][/thing] (400 cards)
[ImageID=7135906] [b]Big box expansions[/b] Many heroes, villains, masterminds, and schemes. About 350-400 cards each. [thing=223362][/thing] [thing=193513][/thing] [thing=137762][/thing] [thing=248084][/thing]
[b]Small box expansions[/b] Five heroes, a few villains, two masterminds and associated schemes. About 100 cards each. [thing=255616][/thing] [thing=186845][/thing] [thing=200983][/thing] [thing=239469][/thing] [thing=231037][/thing] [thing=142020][/thing] [thing=163106][/thing] [thing=149922][/thing]
That's about 3600 cards if my math is right.
In addition, I still have all original boxes stored in a closet if you are interested in acquiring those as well. They take up a lot of space, but you wouldn't be interested in this collection anyway without being local to the con or with a large transport vehicle.
[imageid=7135911 inline] [ImageID=7135907 inline]
[B]FP:[/B] $400

I'll be at the meetup.
[-]$90[/-] SOLD to [user=talon13][/user]
item.comment: I know it's asking for a lot of work, but if i post a jpeg of all the minis any way you could just X out what has been taken out? Or at least how many minis there are?

[q="talon13"]I know it's asking for a lot of work, but if i post a jpeg of all the minis any way you could just X out what has been taken out? Or at least how many minis there are?[/q]
There are 189 individual bags plus a packaged for retail Kickstarter Sophie metal mini. Some of the individual bags contain 2,3,4 and in one case 12 actual minis, generally goblins or rats or smaller figs that come in sets, making the total a bit higher.
For context the figured I removed were for playing the original Pathfinder Adventure Card Game. I took some minis from this package and some from the Pathfinder RPG Starter box. I don't imagine more than 3-4 minis were removed, but I have since gotten rid of both the Card Game and the Starter Box so I can't verify.

[q="talon13"]I'll take them![/q]
Sounds good. See you next month!

I'll accept cash or PayPal. I may consider other offers for this item.
item.comment: Wow! I had never heard of this. Looks amazing. Twelve hour playtime is nuts! Someone buy this and play it at the con so I can come gawk like I do for the large [thing=193949][/thing] games! 😀

[q="wilsonza"]Wow! I had never heard of this. Looks amazing. Twelve hour playtime is nuts! Someone buy this and play it at the con so I can come gawk like I do for the large [thing=193949][/thing] games! 😀[/q]
I actually was able to play a full game of it one year at a convention. It was a heck of an experience - we did indeed play for 12+ hours, and we had to eventually just call it as we were entering the wee morning hours the day after starting. One other player and myself were the clear leaders. The other player kindly offered to call it a tie, although I think he would have won out had we gone full distance to the end. We stumbled back home and slept very soundly after that.

[q="skalpol"]I'll buy it for $300 ![/q]
Thank you Sam - sold, and I hope it gives you many hours of enjoyment. 🙂
See you in November.

[q="wilsonza"]Wow! I had never heard of this. Looks amazing. Twelve hour playtime is nuts! Someone buy this and play it at the con so I can come gawk like I do for the large [thing=193949][/thing] games! 😀[/q] On the 18XX Geeklist 18OE is going on Thursday at the Con. Sanger Room.

item.comment: Quick suggestion: If "un sold" means still available you might want to change the wording as the various list aggregator tools see the word "sold" and assume it's, well, sold. 🙂 Use words like "available again" or "still available" if that's what you mean by "un sold".

Thanks. I am in the process of packing for the con and pulling these without deleting the item - I thought that was the best way (at least that's what I've done in the past) to remove them from the query tools without deleting from the list.

So new problem with this method. Tables are given to people based on sold games now. Unsold marks the item as sold to the aggregator inflating your sell amount.
you need to use +remove+-remove- so that it simply removes them and doesn't mark them sold

You are putting way too much thought into it. They are exactly the same. There is no difference.

Ok. Please note that when you post two items and one is listed for twice as much as the other people are going to question what makes the second item worth more to you the seller (i.e. it is a deluxe version, or is in better condition). Have great day.

[q="steentx"]Ok. Please note that when you post two items and one is listed for twice as much as the other people are going to question what makes the second item worth more to you the seller (i.e. it is a deluxe version, or is in better condition). Have great day.[/q]

I am well aware that gouging is something people do (like every business after covid), I just didn’t think anyone in our community would do that. I hope you sell all your games and savor all the spoils!

Item: My Village Condition: Like New (Cards in shrink, tokens and boards unpunched, never played) Price: $10
Description There's a story on this one. I bought this at a previous VFM because I really enjoy the older cousin ([thing=104006][/thing]). When I got the game home I opened it and the tiles were not punched and the cards were still in shrink wrap, but there were supposed to be 70 black cylinder tokens and I counted only 65. I even posted about it [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/3053823/component-question-manual-says-70-black-cylinders]here[/url].
Later I had the opportunity to buy a brand new shrink-wrapped copy, so I did. That rendered my extra (incomplete) copy redundant. I decided to list it on the VFM and disclose that it was missing cylinders, so I counted again.
There are no missing parts.
I counted 70 black cylinders.
So you have the opportunity to get a nearly new copy of My Village that has shrink wrapped cards, unpunched tokens, and 70, yes, I counted them three times, 70 wooden cylinders and all other parts are also accounted for.

Item: Prophecy Bundle: Base Game (Open) + Dragon Expansion (NIS) Condition: See below Price: $35 Offers Considered
Description This is another game where I've picked up multiple copies over the years. The base game is in excellent condition; the board is nice and glossy and the cards look like they have barely been played, if at all. There is extremely minimal box wear on the game box. That's the good. When I purchased this copy I did an inventory (as I always do!) and discovered it's missing one "magic" cube. There are 40 red plastic strength cubes but only 39 blue plastic magic cubes. I planned to purchase wooden cubes to replace both the red and blue but before doing that I acquired another copy.
This bundle also includes the [thing=26218]Dragon Realm Expansion[/thing] which is brand new in shrink wrap.
Exchange notes: :arrowE: I will be attending BGG Fall. This was the run where the yellow minis were shipped sort of greasy. When cleaning the minis in alcohol we made the mistake of adding the cubes in as well, so the dye faded a bit & one has a tiny piece of paper towel stuck to it that we decided to not attempt to remove for fear of further damaging the cube. I will attempt to get a picture up later today.
Appreciate the info. I can live this with for this price. No pics needed. Consider my $10 official! Thanks!

My notes about the damage were apparently a bit inaccurate. It seems several had stuck to a paper towel, but my wife has made efforts to clean the cubes up. In the ordered photo I set what is in my opinion the "ugliest" side up and in the other I shook the cubes up and tossed them on the table for a more realistic example of what they will look like when randomly viewed.

Item: Folklore Bundle Condition: New Price: [-]$125[/-] Make me an offer! +sold+ traded to [user=punkin312][/user]
Description The asking price is well below what I paid for this several years ago. There have been some other expansions / updates since then, but I think this is still an excellent deal if someone is looking for an open RPG style board game.
[thing=159504]Folklore: The Affliction[/thing] [thing=225525]Folklore: The Affliction – Dark Tales Expansion[/thing] [thing=204088]Folklore: The Affliction – Ghost Miniatures Pack[/thing] [thing=274729]Folklore: The Affliction – Missing Card Pack[/thing]
This bundle includes all of the above but the detailed list below is what you will receive. BGG didn't have links for everything (or I could not find them). Instead I have included the Folklore SKUs (part numbers) so you can do more research if needed.
FL21 - Folklore (1E) Deluxe Experience ($199.95, details below) FL47 - Missing Card Pack (Free, basically) FL42 - Folklore 2E Upgrade Pack ($44.95) FL45 - Story Teller Screen ($14.95) Resin Folklore Colossal Dark Oak ($25, extra figure, not required for game play, just for fun)
The Folklore (First Edition) Deluxe Experience (FL21 KS Bundle) includes all of the following, along with various KS exclusives: FL01 - Core Game ($99) FL02 - Dark Tales ($99) FL05 - Ghost pack ($25) FL06 - Grey miniatures pack ($25) FL07 - Tan Miniatures pack ($40) FL10 - Encounter pad ($10) FL11 - Character Pad ($10)
I had packaged this all up to ship at one point, and I did not open the box to re-verify the contents. If anyone is interested, I will go back and open the box and re-confirm that everything I listed above is available. I would of course expect you to inspect / review everything prior to your purchase. If you have any questions, please ask.
Exchange notes: :arrowE: I will be attending BGG Fall. If I do not qualify for a seller table I will be flexible as to when to meet for an exchange. :arrowE: I accept PayPal Friends and Family once you have had the opportunity to inspect your purchase. I also accept Venmo or Cash. :arrowE: I use [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/wiki/page/Condition_of_a_game]this article[/url] for determining the condition of the items I have for sale.
+altname+ Folklore Bundle -altname-

I believe by the previous post of mine it is the 1st edition.
Found a website that says the box would have a crown with 2.1e in it on top right. Mine does not have that. Changing picture to reflect that and adding it to description.

Item: Shadows Over Camelot with Merlin Expansion Condition: Very Good Price: [-]$245[/-] $225
Description Shadows Over Camelot with the Merlin expansion stored in the base game box only. The expansion box is not available. This is one of my favorite hidden traitor games. Trust me, it's plenty brutal even as a cooperative game.
Before anyone asks, no, I am unfortunately not interested in splitting out the expansion and base game separately.
Detailed Condition Notes The Merlin expansion has never been played. The white cards from the expansion have been opened, but the black cards have not (still in shrink). This game could be a poster child for why sleeving games is useful. The edges of the standard white cards for the base game definitely have a gray tinge to them compared to the unused Merlin white cards. Because these cards are such good quality (Days of Wonder makes good games) I have previously had success with taking a damp rag and cleaning the cards; I have not done that to this copy yet. The box has very minimal shelf wear in my opinion. The plastic inserts that hold the miniatures and catapults and stuff are not present but everything is in plastic baggies. The bonus "orange" knight cards, die, and mini are there (they come with the Merlin expansion).
If you have any questions or want pictures of the card edges let me know.

It is the Special Edition (Gameplay All-in) Sundrop Version pledge, purchased through a retail backer (hence the higher price). item.comment: I know much lower than what you are asking, but throwing out $100 offer. I believe another copy sold for $120?

I appreciate the offer but I have not seen a listing that includes all of what I am offering. I am an idiot and did the alllllllll-in. This is literally everything from the campaign because it was one of my favorite PC games. I just found out later that it's supposedly best solo and I don't do solo gaming. The main box for this thing is seriously something like 4 feet long by 2 feet across. It holds the playmat and all of the main boxes along with all of the other add-ons. $120 would barely cover my shipping for this monstrosity. :) Also, not joking, I would need two people to properly carry this into the convention in lieu of looking like a bumbling buffoon trying to carry it alone. This is way more than even their highest Kickstarter tier that was offered because I got all of the add-ons for it post-campaign. I hope that helps you understand the price difference.

Totally understand! If I had some stuff you would want to trade or partial trade for, I could work something out.... but $250 is a little steep as I am probably in the same situation where its going to sit a long time before it gets played :D

item.comment: Is this the 2nd Edition? I'll buy for $20 if it is.

Not sure how to tell, but someone mentioned in the forum that the cover of the second edition should have: Design by HAL ECCLES Writers include Tim Uren, Jason Maxwell, Will Kenyon & Ben Pharr
I can confirm that my copy does have these names on the front, but I can’t confirm if that means it’s the second edition or not. It also has the 8th Summit logo in the corner. Let me know if there’s something else I can check. I can also post a pic if requested.
Does it have the Grey Fox games logo on it the front cover? I think that is one way to definitely tell.

No, just the 8th Summit logo. Here' what the [thread=2804121]forum here[/thread] says: [i]Yes, that's how I determined my copy was 2nd edition, at least.
It has the 8th Summit logo in the bottom right corner. In the bottom centre it says: Design by HAL ECCLES Writers include Tim Uren, Jason Maxwell, Will Kenyon & Ben Pharr
I believe the 1st edition looks similar except in place of 5 names, it only has 2 and doesn't specify their credits: HALL ECCLES WILL KENYON[/i]
Ok, I'm fairly certain that is still the 2nd Edition. It appears several of the 2nd Edition were released without the Grey Fox logo. I'll take it.
Excellent. I will say we played the first case, and I didn't notice any typos.

Item: Robot Quest Arena KS Bundle Condition: New In Shrink Price: [-]$175[/-] $160 Firm Price
Description This bundle includes everything (I think) except for the sleeves for the recent KS campaign. Included items are all in shrink. [thing=304668][/thing] [thing=379860][/thing] [thing=379861][/thing] [thing=379859][/thing] [thing=379862][/thing]
Here's the story on this item (if anyone cares LOL). I frequently will pick up items at Common Ground and ship them for folks that don't live in the DFW area. Common Ground is a fantastic store, with an awesome selection, but they don't ship. This is the first time I've been unhappy with the process as I purchased the item and then the buyer backed out. Normally I ask the buyer to buy the item and then I just pick up and ship but I was getting two of these bundles so I figured what the heck.
Anyway, my buy-in cost for this with tax for the entire package was basically $160. I listed at $175 to allow someone to make an offer at $160 and I would say, "Sure, I can do that" and we both walk away feeling good about the deal. 🙂 But at the very least I can return the purchase back to the store, so I am not willing to take less than this. If you're interested in the sleeve packs I can pick those up for you too (added cost of course).
Basically I will sell this at $160 or simply return it back to the store. Now you know the story!
Exchange notes: :arrowE: I will be attending BGG Fall. If I do not qualify for a seller table I will be flexible as to when to meet for an exchange. :arrowE: I accept PayPal Friends and Family once you have had the opportunity to inspect your purchase. I also accept Venmo or Cash. :arrowE: I use [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/wiki/page/Condition_of_a_game]this article[/url] for determining the condition of the items I have for sale. +altname+ Robot Quest Arena KS Bundle -altname-

Fun compact, great travel game!
All components in great condition! I do not expect to have a sellers’ table inside the VFM, I will be outside the VFM on Thursday from 6:00-7:00pm and would like to exchange then.[/-]

ITEM WITHDRAWN
[b]Version[/b]: 1.5 [b]Language[/b]: English [b]Condition[/b]: New, cards are in shrink. Models ready to build. Price: [-]$1000[/-] [-]$980[/-] [-]$970[/-] (I know that 4 figure price was scaring some people. Now it is lower!)
Contains the following expansions: Expansion of Death Vol. 1 (all of the expansions: 12/13 in all, Dragon King, Dung Beetle Knight, Lion Knight, Role Survivors, Flower Knight, Manhunter, Gorm, Slenderman, Sunstalker, Lonely Tree, Spidicules, Green Knight, and Lion God) AND the Gambler's Chest (Huge expansion, many variants, lots of miniatures) AND the Campaigns of Death Expansion (new rules, new campaigns) - when it ships.
This is an incredible price because I don't want to have to ship it. And you don't want to have to pay for shipping. The base game is open, but incredibly lightly played. I think I have it back the way it came and would be surprised if you did not find it like opening a new box. The other expansions are still in their original shipping boxes.
So why am I selling? Because I just cannot dedicate the table space and time. It looks great, but it is difficult. I have not painted anything and most models are ready to be assembled.
This price is lower than any I could find for this set.
item.comment: Tried to get a lone from the bank for this. They turned me down :(
If I didnt own all of this, I would be all over it 🙂 my #1 game of all time, amazing price. just had to chime in. Good luck with the sale.
Do you have campaigns of death expansion in hand? I didnt think that was out yet, what are you referring to?

I think you are correct, but I am not sure. I thought it was in the Gambler's Chest. If it is not, then I will have them ship it to the buyer. Or the Buyer can pay postage and I will ship it to them. But it is included in the price if it is not in the Gambler's Chest.
Gotcha, yep, it supposed to come end of this year, so as we all know that means we should have it by 2026 😆

2026? No doubt!
But I must say the quality of this game is beyond reproach. You just have to wait until it is done.

Item: Masmorra KS Condition: Like New Price: Make Offer
Description I opened the box and found a bunch of notes about it including KS bonus stuff. I am going to list this and price it once I finish figuring out what all is here, because I am sure potential buyers will want to know...so subscribe for updates if you're interested. :)
I had forgotten that I had not updated this yet until someone sent me a Geek Mail. My apologies. Here are more detailed notes about the game contents and condition.
There are 25 minis. There are three sets of dice. Once set looks like the normal d6 size and there are 39 of those. 36 of them look like they might be player-color dice as there are six different colors of dice that seem to match. Red, Yellow, Green, Purple, Black and Blue. Then there are 3 more white dice. I don't know if there were supposed to be six white dice or just 3, that's one of of the things that confused me when I last opened the box. These dice are all in a zip-lock baggie.
Then there are two specialty dice bags, one orange and one blue. These have larger dice that are different colors. The orange bag has an outline of a dragon head on it and contains four pink, four purple, four orange, four gray and two yellow dice.
The blue bag has an outline of a skull on it. It contains eight green dice, eight light-blue dice, four orange dice and four light red or pink dice.
The cards that have been opened are all sleeved and stored in deck boxes.
There is a package of cards that has not been opened that I think is the Arcadia Quest cross-over deck.
There is a bag with some cardboard money tokens along with a bag of plastic money tokens. There are some cardboard discs that also have poker-chip style acrylic replacements. There is a bag of plastic treasure chests.
Here is what I wrote down on my notes when I bought the game.
Adventurers Set Monster Dice Set Luck the Lucky Promo Dice Arcadia Crossover Colored Action Dice Treasure Chest Pack Plastic Token Pack
The game looks like it was never played. Everything is in pristine condition. As mentioned the cards are sleeved (premium sleeves, not thinner penny sleeves). Everything has been stored in baggies. The acrylic token pack is cool too. The high price point on eBay was almost three hundred dollars for an equivalent package that was still in shrink. This is not in shrink but still essentially brand new. I am not looking for that level of pricing just so you know, just mentioning it as a data point. :)
If this is enough information for someone to make an offer, feel free! Just know that the person who contacted me via Geek Mail is first in line. Thanks!
